sections.title: Responsible AI as a design requirement

blocks.heading: Earlier is cheaper
paragraphs: Retrofitting responsible AI after deployment typically costs 3–5× as much as building it in. We integrate fairness testing, explainability and documentation into development so issues are found before they reach customers.

blocks.heading: Scope follows your obligations
paragraphs: The right scope depends on which frameworks apply to your systems — sector rules such as HIPAA or FCRA, the EU AI Act, NYC Local Law 144 for automated employment decision tools, or voluntary alignment with the NIST AI RMF. Shared governance frameworks and documentation templates reduce the marginal cost for each additional system.

blocks.heading: What we do not provide
paragraphs: We do not make definitive regulatory compliance determinations or provide legal strategy. Those require qualified legal counsel; we supply the technical analysis, implementations and documentation that counsel and auditors rely on.

sections.title: Questions about responsible AI and compliance

items.question: How much does responsible AI compliance cost?
items.answer: $20,000–$220,000 depending on regulatory scope and number of systems. Most single-system responsible AI engagements run $30,000–$80,000.

items.question: How long does responsible AI compliance take?
items.answer: Individual components: 4–14 weeks. Full responsible AI programs: 16–32 weeks.

items.question: How does bias testing work?
items.answer: Statistical tests compare prediction distributions across protected class groups using standardized methods — the 4/5ths rule, statistical significance testing and effect size measurement. Findings and remediation options are documented.

items.question: Can you audit AI systems we already run?
items.answer: Yes — we assess the deployed model, test for disparate impact, evaluate explainability and produce a remediation priority report.

items.question: Do you provide EU AI Act compliance certification?
items.answer: No. We prepare the technical documentation and implementation that EU AI Act compliance requires. Conformity assessment is conducted by notified bodies, and compliance determinations require qualified legal counsel.

items.question: We don't have regulatory obligations — do we still need this?
items.answer: Voluntary NIST AI RMF alignment and internal governance frameworks ($25,000–$65,000) still reduce operational and reputational risk, and make later regulatory work cheaper.

sections.heading: Understand your responsible AI scope
sections.text: Tell us which AI systems you run or plan to launch, where they are used and who they affect. An engineer will reply within one business day with the components that likely apply and a budget range.
